html.body: Date: 2025-03-21 REMARKSThis paper is filed in response to the Office Action mailed January 8, 2025 (hereinafter "Office Action") in connection with the above-referenced application. By way of summary, claims 1-2, 4-5, and 8-20 were pending in this application. In this paper, Applicant has canceled claims without prejudice or disclaimer, amended claims without prejudice or disclaimer to their previously presented versions, and added claims. No new matter is added. Applicant reserves the right to pursue the previously pending claims and/or subject matter of the previously pending claims in this or another application. Accordingly, claims 1, 4-5, 8-12, 14-16, 18, and 21-36 are pending for consideration.Discussion of Allowable Subject Matter Claims 5 and 20 are objected to as being dependent upon a rejected base claim, but would be allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims. Applicant thanks the Examiner for recognizing the allowability of the claims. Applicant acknowledges the Examiner's statements regarding the allowable subject matter and agrees that the claimed subject matter is patentable. However, any statements in the Office Action should not be attributed to Applicant as an indication of why Applicant believes the claims are patentable. Furthermore, Applicant respectfully asserts that there also may be reasons for patentability of the claimed subject matter not explicitly stated in this record, and Applicant does not waive its rights to such arguments by not further addressing such reasons herein. To the extent that there is any implication in the statements that the patentability of the claims rests on the recitation of a single feature or the combination of particular features in a particular claim, Applicant respectfully disagrees because patentability rests on each claim taken as a whole.Applicant additionally respectfully reserves the right to traverse the characterizations of what any particular reference teaches or suggests, of what any combination of references teaches or suggests, or the appropriateness of combining references.In this Reply, Applicant has amended independent claim 1 to incorporate certain recitations from dependent claims 2 and 20, as well as added independent claim 23 to incorporate certain recitations from dependent claim 5. In light of at least these amendments, Applicant believes that the application is in condition for immediate allowance and respectfully requests the same.Discussion of Claim Rejections Under 35 U.S.C. 103 Claims 1-7, 9-11, 16-19 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over U.S. Publication No. 20190090766 to Block et al. ("Block"), cited previously, in view of U.S.Publication No. 20160058309 to Han ("Han").Claim 8 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Block in view of Han as applied to claim 1 above, and further in view of U.S. Patent No. 11857298 to Allee ("Allee"), cited previously.Claims 12-15 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Block in view of Han as applied to claim 1 above, and further in view of U.S. Patent No. 10987054 to Pandya ("Pandya"), cited previously.Applicant respectfully traverses each rejection, each finding of fact, including each assertion regarding what the references show or teach, and any rationales for modifying or combining the references, and Applicant does not acquiesce in the validity of the rejections.The Office Action acknowledges that "Block does not specifically show a light barrier construct mounted on the substrate and defining a first emitter chamber that houses the first emitter group of LEDs, and a second emitter chamber that houses the second emitter group of LEDs, wherein the light barrier construct is configured to optically isolate the first emitter group of LEDs from the second emitter group of LEDs" but then relies on at least FIG. 6A of Han as allegedly remedying these deficiencies (Office Action at pg. 3), which is reproduced below in part.As shown above, Han FIG. 6A and other portions fail to teach or suggest "a first emitter chamber that houses the first emitter group of LEDs, and a second emitter chamber that houses the second emitter group of LEDs, wherein the light barrier construct is configured to optically isolate the first emitter group ofLEDs from the second emitter group ofLEDs" as recited in claim 1 (emphasis added). The other cited references fail to remedy the deficiencies of Block and Han.Thus, the cited references, alone or in combination, fail to teach or suggest each of the recitations of claim 1. Thus, claim 1 is not obvious in light of any combination of the cited references for at least the reasons discussed.Nevertheless, to expedite allowance of this application, Applicant has amended the claims as set forth herein. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of each rejection. Amended independent claim 1 recites the following:An optical physiological sensor integrated into a wearable device, the optical physiological sensor comprising:a substrate having an optical center;a first emitter group of light emitting diodes (LEDs) positioned adjacent to the optical center of the substrate and spaced at an offset from the optical center;a second emitter group of LEDs positioned adjacent to the optical center of the substrate at an offset to the optical center and spaced at an offset from the optical center opposite the first emitter group of LEDs relative to the optical center;a plurality of detectors arranged in an annular spatial configuration that surrounds the first emitter group and the second emitter group, wherein each of the plurality of detectors are positioned on the substrate a same distance away from the optical center of the substrate, wherein the annular spatial configuration has a radius of less than 6.75mm; and a light barrier construct mounted on the substrate and defining a first emitter chamber that houses the first emitter group of LEDs, and a second emitter chamber that houses the second emitter group of LEDs, wherein the light barrier construct is configured to optically isolate the first emitter group of LEDs from the second emitter group of LEDs.Because the cited references, alone or in combination, fail to teach or suggest each of the recitations of amended independent claim 1 and new claim 23, Applicant respectfully submits that amended claim 1, and newly presented claim 23, are allowable over the cited references. The dependent claims are also allowable for all of the reasons discussed above with respect to one of claims 1 or 23 and also because each of these claims recites a unique combination of features not taught or suggested by the cited references, alone or in combination. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103.No Disclaimers or Disavowals Although the present communication may include alterations to the application or claims, or characterizations of claim scope or referenced art, Applicant is not conceding in this application that previously pending claims are not patentable. Rather, any alterations or characterizations are being made to facilitate expeditious prosecution of this application. Applicant reserves the right to pursue at a later date any previously pending or other broader or narrower claims that capture any subject matter supported by the present disclosure, including subject matter found to be specifically disclaimed herein or by any prior prosecution. Accordingly, reviewers of this or any parent, child or related prosecution history shall not reasonably infer that Applicant has made any disclaimers or disavowals of any subject matter supported by the present application.Please charge any additional fees, including any fees for additional extension of time, or credit overpayment to Deposit Account No. 11-1410.Respectfully submitted, KNOBBE, MARTENS, OLSON & BEAR, LLPDated: March 21, 2025 By: /Spencer Carter/ Spencer Carter Registration No. 76,416 Registered Practitioner (949) 760-0404 60840699
